AgentAttentionEvent.description: `agent.attention` data: an agent needs the user.

msgId.description: The message whose delivery is uncertain, for `mail_uncertain`.

reason.description: Why: a permission prompt, a notification, `mail_uncertain: <msg>`.

toolUseId.description: The hook's `tool_use_id` (may be `null`), for a hook's attention.

AgentCreateParams.description:
`agent.create` params. C1a creates only free agents (A:794): no brief,
no worktree, the given cwd.

cwd.description: An absolute directory. The engine uses its realpath.

kind.description: The adapter kind. Only `claude` in C1a.

name.description:
A display name: letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`, unique among
the live engine agents.

AgentCreateResult.description: `agent.create` result: the agent once it is `ready`.

AgentFailedEvent.description: `agent.failed` data: a managed agent could not be started or kept.

AgentGoneEvent.description: `agent.gone` data: the session behind an observed agent ended.

all.description: Also return gone, retired and failed agents (tombstones included).

AgentRetireResult.description:
`agent.retire` result: the tombstone row (A:828). Retiring a retired or
failed agent changes nothing and returns its row.

AgentRow.description:
One row of the `agents` table (A:340), as `snapshot.get`,
`session.list` and `agent.list` send it.

createdBy.description: The principal that created the agent.

cwd.description: The working directory; for an observed agent, the project path.

generation.description: +1 on spawn, resume, refresh and takeover.

goneAt.description: Unix ms; `null` while the agent is alive.

lastSeen.description:
Unix ms of a detection tick that saw the agent. While nothing else
in the row changes, it moves at most once a minute.

machineId.description: The machine the agent runs on.

parentId.description:
The agent that owns this one; for an imported legacy worker, the PM
that adopted it.

providerSid.description: The provider session id of the current generation.

sessionKey.description:
`SessionIdentity::key()` (`<provider>:<session id>`) of the session
detection matched to this agent.

startedAt.description: Unix ms, as the provider reports it.

state.description:
Engine lifecycle state (`creating`, `starting`, `ready`, `working`,
`blocked`, `paused`, `refreshing`, `interrupted`, `retiring`,
`retired`, `failed`, `orphaned`); `null` for an observed agent.

stateReason.description:
Why the agent is in its `state`: `drain` for a `paused` or
`interrupted` agent that an engine drain stopped; for a `failed`
agent the failure reason, such as `spawn_failed`, `resume_failed`,
`exited` or `create_interrupted`.

by.description: What saw the turn end: `hook` or `screen`.

partial.description:
The index dropped events newer than `since_ms`, so the counts are a
lower bound.

ClientInfo.description: What a client says about itself in `hello`. Unverified.

ConversationGetParams.description:
`conversation.get` params: one session's transcript, as the GUI's
`get_conversation` reads it.

includeTools.description: Keep tool-use and tool-result messages. Default false, as in the GUI.

sessionKey.description:
`<provider>:<session id>`. A bare session id (no known provider
prefix) is looked up in every provider, or in `provider`.

ConversationGetResult.description:
`conversation.get` result. `messages` are the page asked for, in
transcript order. Each call reads the transcript again.

nextOffset.description: `offset` of the next page; `null` after the last one.

images.description: Images attached to this message (screenshots pasted by the user)

CostData.description: Aggregated cost data returned to the frontend.

unpricedTokens.description: Tokens whose provider/model has no local USD pricing table.

DeepSearchHit.description: A single deep-search hit: session ID + first matching snippet (truncated).

snippet.description: Up to 200 chars of context around the first keyword match, from the matching line.

DetectRecheckParams.description:
`detect.recheck` params. There are none yet; the engine ignores any it
gets.

hiddenClaudeSessions.description:
Live Claude Code sessions that Claude Code itself keeps out of its
registry, so c9watch can count them but not show them.

ErrorBody.description: The `error` object of a failed response.

data.description:
Facts about this error for the caller to act on, such as the
`nearest` name for `unknown_address`. Absent for most errors.

ErrorCode.description:
Typed error codes. New codes are additive; a client that does not know a
code still has `msg`, `retryable` and `hint`.

oneOf.description: The client speaks another major version.
The first frame was not `hello`.
No `hello` arrived in time.
A frame is larger than `MAX_FRAME`.
The frame is not valid JSON or misses a required field.
The engine has no such method.
The peer runs under another uid.

The cursor's events are gone: pruned, another epoch or machine, or
ahead of the log.

The caller is over a limit, such as the event streams per
connection.

A hook-class method (`hook.*`, `task.done`, `agent.handoff`) from a
caller that is not a live agent running the engine's own
`c9watch-agent` copy, or that names another agent.
`task.done` from an agent without a task (every free agent).

The method is part of the wire format but does nothing before C1b
(`agent.handoff`).

The engine has no `c9watch-agent` copy: none was next to the engine
binary when it started, or the copy is gone.

The engine's `c9watch-agent` copy no longer has the sha256 it had
when the engine installed it.

The principal may not call this method (`agent.create` and
`agent.retire` take only a local client in C1a).

The canonical cwd of a free agent is inside the engine home or a
managed worktree home.

The agent process exited, showed a vendor refusal (usage limit,
login) or was not ready in time. The engine does not retry.
No engine agent has this id.

The engine is draining after a SIGTERM: no spawn and no injection
until the next engine is up. Retry against the new engine.

`msg.send`: no agent answers to `to`, its machine is not this one,
or a name matches more than one agent. `data` has `nearest` or
`candidates`.

`msg.send`: the engine does not drive the target's terminal (an
observed session), or the target is retiring or gone. `data` has
`state` and `control`.

`msg.send`: a managed worker takes mail only from its parent and
the human, and sends only to its parent. `data` may have `parent`.

`msg.send`: the `idem` key was used for another message, or the same
body went to the same agent within 10 minutes. `data` has `msgId`
and `at`.
`session.stop`: no live session has this key.

`session.stop` or `session.rename` was refused or failed on the
session itself: it cannot be stopped, it runs as another process
now, or the write failed. `msg` says which.

The engine is at a limit that frees up soon: the connection cap, or
a scan of the same kind that is still running. Retry shortly.
An engine-side failure.

EventFrame.description:
One event on the wire (A:203). `sub` is the `id` of the subscribe
request, so a connection can carry several subscriptions.

EventType.description:
The `type` of an event frame. A response frame has no `type`, so a
client tells the two apart by `type === "event"`.

HandoffParams.description:
`agent.handoff` params (`c9watch-agent handoff --note -`). The wire
format is fixed now; the engine answers `unsupported_in_c1a` until C1b.

note.description: What the next generation should know.

seq.description: The sender's clock in ns, as a string.

HelloParams.description:
`hello` params. `client` is the caller's own claim. The engine only logs
it as unverified; it never decides the principal (N1).

apiMinor.description:
The minor the client was built against. `hello.result.breakingSince`
lists the preview methods that changed shape after it. Without it,
the engine assumes minor 0.

breakingSince.description:
The preview methods whose shape changed after the client's
`apiMinor`. A client refuses to call them; it does not guess.

cursor.description: Cursor of the newest committed event. `null` only without a store.

principal.description: Stamped by the engine from connection facts.

stability.description: `preview` until the protocol is declared stable.

topics.description: The event topics this connection can receive.

parentClaudePid.description:
`CLAUDE_PID` from the hidden process: the Claude Code process that
opened the app it runs in, when it's set.

oneOf.description:
The process inherited `CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION`, so Claude Code
turned off its registry entry and transcript.

HistoryEntry.description: A deduplicated, enriched history entry returned to the frontend

aiTitle.description: Claude Code's auto-generated title (`ai-title` in the session JSONL).

codexTitle.description: Codex's current UI thread name from ~/.codex/session_index.jsonl.

cursorTitle.description: Cursor's current UI composer name from state.vscdb.

HistoryListResult.description:
`history.list` result: past sessions of every provider, newest first,
as the GUI's `get_session_history` lists them.

HistorySearchParams.description: `history.search` params: a phrase search over Claude Code transcripts.

HistorySearchResult.description:
`history.search` result: one hit per matching session. A blank query
has none.

HookParams.description:
`hook.*` params: one Claude Code hook event, sent by `c9watch-agent
hook <event>`. The engine alone writes the log (A:1167).

agentId.description: `C9_AGENT_ID` of the sender. It must be the agent the engine stamped.

input.description:
The hook's stdin JSON as the vendor sent it; `null` when it was not
JSON or too large.

kind.description:
The adapter kind of the hook (`claude`). The engine compares it with
the agent row (A:1056).

seq.description: The sender's clock in ns, as a string. With `agentId` it dedupes.

truncated.description: The stdin JSON was larger than the hook forwards.

accepted.description:
The engine took the event. A dropped event (an old generation, a
duplicate) still gets `ok:true`, with `accepted:false`.

additionalContext.description:
For `hook.session_start`: context the hook prints as
`hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext`.

ImageBlock.description:
User message structure

In Claude Code's JSONL format, user message content can be either:
- A plain string (for actual user prompts)
- An array of content blocks (for tool results sent back to Claude)
A base64-encoded image found in a user message content array

LegacyInboxEvent.description: `legacy.inbox` data: one imported worker inbox line, as it was.

id.description: The worker's agent id, when the import found its row.

maxConnections.description: Connections the socket serves at once.

maxFrame.description: Bytes in one frame, newline included.

retentionEvents.description: Events the outbox keeps at most.

retentionHours.description: Hours the outbox keeps an event.

MemoryFile.description: A single memory file (e.g., MEMORY.md, profile.md)

MemoryListResult.description:
`memory.list` result: memory files grouped by project, as the GUI's
`get_memory_files` reads them.

rev.description: Goes up by one on each breaking change to the method's shape.

since.description: The minor that added the method.

MsgAddress.description: The agent a message went to.

MsgKind.description:
What a message asks of its reader (A:418). A caller sends `request` or
`info`; `result` and `system` are written by the engine.

MsgSendParams.description:
`msg.send` params. The envelope's `idem` makes a resend safe: the same
sender, key and request get the first message back.

body.description: UTF-8 text. No control characters other than `\n` and `\t`.

replyTo.description: The id of the message this one answers. Stored, not checked.

to.description:
An agent id (`agt_<ulid>`), a name, or `<machine>/<id>` with this
machine's id.

MsgSendResult.description: `msg.send` result. The response's `seq` is the same cursor.

cursor.description:
Cursor of the message's `msg.state` `queued` event. For a replay it
is the first send's cursor, which may be past event retention.

replayed.description:
The same sender sent the same request with this `idem` before; no
new message was written.

state.description: The message's state now: `queued` for a new message.

MsgStateEvent.description:
`data` of a `msg.state` event: one per state change of a message. The
event's subject is the target's `<machine>/<id>`.

detail.description:
Why: for `delivered`, `prompt_hook` or `turn_open`; for `failed` and
`uncertain`, what went wrong.

NotificationEvent.description:
`notification.needs_attention` and `notification.waiting_for_input`
data: what the GUI shows in its system notification.

id.description: The agent id of the session.

title.description: Can carry conversation text (the first prompt, a session title).

OpenTarget.description: The strongest native target supported by the existing focus mechanism.

OpencodeConnectParams.description:
`provider.opencode.connect` params: the OpenCode server detection
reads. An empty `url` disconnects. The engine keeps the credentials in
memory only and never returns them.

PageParams.description: A window of a list: `limit` items from `offset`.

limit.description: At most this many items; without it, all from `offset`.

ProgressFrame.description:
A `progress` frame: how far a read for request `id` has got. Sent only
to a connection that asked for the `conversation.progress` capability,
before that request's response. Never stored; a slow client may miss
some.

id.description: The `id` of the request it reports on.

ProjectMemory.description: All memory files for a single project

files.description: Memory files found in this project

memoryDirPath.description: Absolute path to the memory directory (for "Reveal in Finder")

projectName.description: Human-readable project name (last path segment, e.g. "c9watch")

provider.description: Provider that owns this memory group. Older payloads default to Claude Code.

Request.description:
A request frame. Every field is optional on the wire, so that a frame
with a missing field still gets an error that echoes its `id`.

Response.description: A response frame: `ok:true` with `result`, or `ok:false` with `error`.

seq.description: Cursor of the event this write produced (from M2).

SessionAwayResult.description:
`session.away` result: what each session did after its `sinceMs`,
keyed by session key. A session without an index (not Claude Code, or
not seen by a detection tick yet) is absent.

SessionCostRecord.description: A single session's cost record (stored in cache).

SessionListParams.description:
`session.list` params. There are none yet; the engine ignores any it
gets.

SessionListResult.description:
`session.list` result: the agents whose session detection sees now
(`goneAt` is `null`), in creation order.

SessionRenameParams.description: `session.rename` params: set a Claude Code session's custom title.

provider.description:
Only `claudeCode`. Without it, an id that another provider also
has is refused.

SessionStatus.description: Represents the current status of a Claude Code session

oneOf.description: Claude is actively executing tools or thinking
Waiting for user attention (tool approval, question, etc.)
Idle, ready for next prompt
Session starting up or no recent activity

SessionStopParams.description:
`session.stop` params: stop an observed Claude Code session with
SIGTERM. The pid comes from the engine's own detection.

pid.description: When given, detection must still see the session as this pid.

sessionId.description: The raw Claude Code session id.

SessionTasksResult.description:
`session.tasks` result: the session's TodoWrite tasks as Claude Code
wrote them, sorted by numeric `id`.

aiTitle.description: Claude Code's auto-generated title (`ai-title` in the session JSONL).

codexTitle.description: Codex's current UI thread name from ~/.codex/session_index.jsonl.

cursorTitle.description: Cursor's current UI composer name from state.vscdb.

entrypoint.description:
Raw `entrypoint` from `~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json` (e.g. "cli", "sdk-cli",
"claude-vscode", "mcp", "remote_desktop"...). Only the CLI backend populates
this; `None` covers the legacy backend and non-Claude-Code providers.

kind.description:
Interactive vs. background-pinned (`claude agents --json`'s `kind`).
Providers other than Claude Code always report `Interactive`.

lastAssistantMessage.description: One-line, tag-free preview of the last assistant text.

officialName.description:
User-set name from `claude agents` (Ctrl+T background-pinned sessions).
Only populated by the CLI backend; legacy backend leaves this None.

openTarget.description: Native target guarantee; absent means no verified exact native target.

pendingToolInput.description: The input/arguments of the pending tool (when status is NeedsPermission)

sessionKey.description: Provider-scoped identity used by frontend selection and backend maps.

sourceHealth.description: Health of the source observation, independent of the session status.

startedAtMs.description:
Session start time in ms since epoch (from `claude agents --json`).
Only populated by the CLI backend; legacy backend leaves this None.

waitingFor.description: What the session needs from the user (tool name only, never arguments).

workerOf.description:
Session ID of the PM that spawned this session (if it's a c9watch worker).
Set by the workers overlay from `~/.claude/c9watch/workers/*/meta.json`
(`session::workers`), after detection.

SessionViewsParams.description:
`session.views` params. There are none yet; the engine ignores any it
gets.

SessionViewsResult.description:
`session.views` result: the sessions of the last detection tick, as the
GUI shows them, in detection order, and the cursor they are consistent
with. Subscribing to `session.*` with `since` = `cursor` continues with
no gap: `session.view` carries a new or changed session in full,
`session.gone` (`SessionGoneEvent`) one that ended.

SnapshotParams.description:
`snapshot.get` params. There are none yet; the engine ignores any it
gets.

SnapshotResult.description:
`snapshot.get` result: the state and the cursor it is consistent with.
Subscribing with `since` = `cursor` continues with no gap.

SourceHealth.description:
Health of the source observation used to produce a session card.

This is deliberately separate from `SessionStatus`: a session can be
waiting for input while its source is fresh, partial, or unavailable.

SubagentInfo.description: A subagent invocation found in a parent session's JSONL.

completedAt.description: ISO-8601 timestamp when the tool_result was recorded (None if still running).

description.description: Short description of the task (`description` field of Agent tool input).

id.description: The Agent tool's `tool_use_id` — unique within the parent session.

startedAt.description: ISO-8601 timestamp when the tool_use was recorded.

SubagentListParams.description:
`subagent.list` params: the raw Claude Code session ids the caller
shows (not session keys).

SubagentListResult.description: `subagent.list` result: parent session id → its subagent invocations.

SubagentTranscript.description:
Full transcript of a single subagent invocation — the prompt (Agent tool
input), the final result text, and usage stats when available.

agentId.description: Internal agent id from `toolUseResult.agentId` (CC sub-agent handle).

prompt.description: Prompt sent to the subagent (from the Agent tool_use input).

result.description:
Final result text from the subagent, if completed. Concatenation of
text blocks in the matching tool_result content array, preferring
`toolUseResult.content[].text` when present.

since.description:
The last cursor the client has seen. Without it, the stream starts at
the current head.

topics.description: Exact topics, or a prefix ending in `.*` (`agent.*`).

SubscribeResult.description:
`events.subscribe` result. Event frames follow it on the same
connection until the connection closes, or until an error frame with
the subscribe request's `id` (`cursor_expired` when the subscriber fell
behind retention).

cursor.description: Where the stream starts: events after this cursor follow.

seq.description: The sender's clock in ns, as a string.

TaskDoneResult.description:
`task.done` result. In C1a every agent is free, so the call fails with
`no_task` instead.

TickResult.description:
`detect.recheck`, `session.stop` and `session.rename` result. The call
ran one detection tick before it answered: its `session.view` and
`session.gone` events are at or before `cursor`.

backend.description: The detection backend after the tick: `cli` or `legacy`.

UnsubscribeResult.description: `events.unsubscribe` result. No event frame of the stream follows it.

ended.description: `false` when the connection held no stream with that `sub`.

UsageSubscriptionsResult.description:
`usage.subscriptions` result: one snapshot per provider plan. The
engine reads the providers at most once a minute.

windowSeconds.description: Full window length, so the UI can show how far into the window `now` is.

WaitingFor.description:
What a session needs from the user. Tool arguments are never included:
only the tool *name* leaves the backend.

description: The c9watch engine protocol: one JSON object per line over the engine socket. Within a major version every change is additive.
title: c9p/1

session.view.description: Latest state: the log keeps only the newest view of each live session (and none of an ended one). A subscriber that reads on from an old cursor gets the newest view of every live session, not every view in between. Live subscribers still get each view as it is written.
